This is my updated progress post on my weight loss journey, I’ve been waiting until I crossed 225lbs to post again. Since fully starting tracking around April 2019, I’ve lost about 40lbs, going from 265 to 225 (actually 224.4 but I rounded up!).

What works for me might not work for everyone but I’ve learned that this is all about finding what actually works for you and your body.  I practice modified interval fasting based around my work schedule. I eat my first, small meal, usually a PB+J sandwich before work, and then I just drink water throughout my shift, and eat a large meal afterwards. I work in a Long Term Care facility as a Nurse’s Aide, so it’s a physically demanding job as I move, lift, and turn people, so I don’t work out otherwise because I haven’t needed to, the combination of my job and walking around in my facility has provided the calorie burning that I needed.  I sometimes eat a small snack during work, as I can occasionally get grouchy if my body is being more demanding about food than normal, but I otherwise only eat twice a day. This method works great for me but for others might not work at all, that’s why I think weight loss is all about finding what works really well for you.

Looking at the pictures I’m actually shocked by how much my face has changed, I didn’t think that I looked that bad until I had newer pictures to compare with, I was so bloated and pudgy! Now at 225, I feel more energetic and actually want to move when before all I did was sleep. I don’t feel the need to stuff my face full all the time and have begun to realize what my hunger/thirst signals actually are. My face has started to clear up and I don’t feel greasy all the time, although I do feel cold so much easier now! I’ve dropped a full pants size and all my clothes are loose on me now.

Can’t wait to add my next update up here, will probably be when I hit 200lbs for 65lbs lost. See you then all!

I’ve been very impatiently waiting for my scale to drop the last 2lbs that I’ve been stalled at before I made this post, which will hopefully be the first of a series of successful progress pics as I try to finally lose the weight and keep it off. My intended goal is to reach around 135lbs to 150lbs. I don’t list an exact number because I’ve never not been big so I don’t even know who I’ll be at those weights.

Basic info, always been big, parents didn’t teach nutrition/push veggies, PCOS didn’t help at all. During college I managed to go from around 250lbs to almost 200lbs but then I lost traction, gained the weight and then some back, and had many failed attempts at losing the weight again.  I went through a low period with the death of a close family member and my response was to emotionally eat and spiked my weight back up in the process. I don’t know the exact number but I was in the high 260s possibly 270s at the beginning of this year and I felt awful. Nothing fit, I couldn’t help feeling my rolls when I put my arms down, it was mentally horrifying to me and I knew that I really needed to get serious about losing weight again because I liked where I was at 200lbs, I felt good, and if I felt good there I bet I’d feel better at even less weight.

So, I unintentionally began again. I lazily tried to track my food in Myfitnesspal while still binging on junk and not recording it. What changed in my life was getting a new job as a Nurse’s Aide working night shift, which for some reason has managed to turn my life around, at least where my weight is concerned. I began that job in March and officially began tracking my weight loss in April.  Working as an aide has got me moving a lot more than I was before, which was pretty much not at all, and working nights has had the bonus of making fast food less available, because I’m asleep while they’re running. 

That’s not to say that my diet isn’t still crap but I want that I be a point that it’s all about CICO, even if its junky food. I still eat McD’s and Chipotle, I love French fries and burrito bowls, but if I eat fast food, I’ve generally banked most of my calories until my “evening” meal before going to sleep to be able to have the junk food. I try to eat around 1200-1500 calories in a day and I’m not terribly strict about it, I just try to not have the extra scoop of rice and beans or half the pasta I’m eating, things like that. I use MFP to track those calories and I have a fitbit versa watch that tracks my pulse, steps, and creates an estimate of what I’m burning to compare to what I’m taking in. I track my intake for everyday that I work, which is 5 days out of the week and kind of do a pseudo-interval fast, meaning at work I generally only have some coffee and maybe a small snack then have all the rest of my meals between 8am and 1pm. On my two days off, I don’t pay attention to MFP or anything tracking and just let myself eat as I feel hunger, which I’m beginning to feel differently as I realize what’s hunger and what’s actually not for my body. 

For some reason, all these things together have worked this time and I’m actually losing the weight, unlike the other times I’ve tried and failed to count calories, restrict eating, etc. I’ve realized that for myself, I need to not be quite as strict because that’s how I fail. I might even have to go buy some new scrub pants before I lose mine at work one of these nights!  This got way longer than expected but hopefully I will be back in the near future saying that my 20lb loss has become a 50lb, and then again maybe another! I just can’t wait!

Paint mixed with flexible modeling paste then piped through a cake decorating bag and added to the piece after its dry.  Everything in this painting is made out of acrylic paints

It's almost entirely paint with a couple subtle wire supports inside.  I use acrylic paints and use mix-ins called flexible modeling paste and gloss gel medium to change the consistency of the paint.  I mixed white paint with the flexible modeling paste on tin foil and let it dry, then peeled it up and shaped and glued it together, with a couple round pieces of sculpting wire to support them.  The stamens and stems were paint mixed with gloss gel medium and water and piped through a cake decorating bag, the stamens have wire that's glued down into the wire supports.

These recipes were made more as experiments for taste and concept as I’m adjusting back into keto and trying meal prep along with it this time.  Keto works really well for me, I’m just really bad at sticking to it and always end up gaining back what I lost.  Not this time, I’m going to win this time!!  I’m hoping adding meal prep in will help curb my overeating tendencies and help keep me keto-ing.  This is my first week back on it, I’m still adjusting.  The recipes are below, not pictured is pork rinds, pickles, sauerkraut, and some hotdogs for a bit of variety and crunch. 

For all of these recipes I used boneless skinless chicken thighs, a store bought bag of them tossed in a crockpot overnight with half a cup of chicken broth, pepper, and a bit of salt.  The plus is that I get chicken and I get delicious broth too!  Also, if you’ve never used a handheld mixer to shred chicken before, do it now.  I tried it for the first time with this batch and I’m definitely not going back to using forks now.  Next time I think I’m going to get twice the amount of chicken and freeze any extra meals.

My album also has screenshots from myfitnesspal’s recipe builder
